title: Dynamics 365 Business Central: design custom AI agents with the AI development toolkit
summary: The briefing's controls, default state and consumption licensing are supported. Both deterministic warnings are resolved by the documentation: the feature-selection step is present, and the allocation endpoint is assembled from documented URL variables. Two checklist items name controls missing from the controls table.

claims.quote: Searched: Business Central Copilot capabilities API activate deactivate; "Copilot Capability" "Activate". Opened enable-ai and System.AI.Copilot-Capability reference; registration and status inspection exist, but no capability activation/deactivation method is documented.

claims.claim: Search (Alt+Q) opens the Copilot & agent capabilities page.

claims.claim: The design capability is listed under Production ready previews.
claims.quote: The design capability is listed under **Production ready previews**.

claims.claim: The general cross-geography control is Business Central > Copilot & agent capabilities > Allow data movement toggle.
claims.quote:
enter **Copilot & agent capabilities**, and then choose the related link.
2. Switch the **Allow data movement** toggle on or off as desired.

claims.claim: No API for the Business Central Allow data movement toggle is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Business Central "Allow data movement" "API"; Business Central "Allow data movement" codeunit. Opened enable-ai, ai-copilot-data-movement and Copilot Capability reference; no setter API for this toggle was documented.

claims.claim: The toggle appears only when a capability might process data outside the environment's Azure geography.
claims.quote: The **Allow data movement** toggle appears when one or more copilot and agent capabilities might process data in a different Azure geography from the Business Central environment.

claims.claim: The documentation does not explicitly identify Custom Agent as governed by Allow data movement.
claims.quote: Searched: "Custom Agent" "data movement". Opened enable-ai, ai-copilot-data-movement and toolkit overview. The setting covers Microsoft-managed AI processing generally; none explicitly places Custom Agent in that processing class.

claims.claim: Capacity allocation is reached through Power Platform admin center > Licensing > Products > Copilot Studio > Summary > Prepaid capacity > Manage Capacity.
claims.quote:
In the **Licensing** pane, under **Products**, select **Copilot Studio**.
4. Select the **Summary** tab.
5. Complete one of the following actions:

    - Select **Manage Capacity** from the **Prepaid capacity** card.

claims.claim: PUT licensing/allocationsV2 with API version 2024-10-01, environment scope and MCSMessages quantity allocates Copilot Credits.
claims.quote:
Invoke-RestMethod -Method Put `
    -Uri "$apiBaseUrl/licensing/allocationsV2?api-version=$apiVersion" `
    -Headers $headers -ContentType "application/json" -Body $allocationBody

claims.claim: An environment allocation applies to Business Central after linking it to the Power Platform environment.
claims.quote: Once completed, consumption of the Copilot Credits in the Business Central environment is limited by the capacity allocated to the linked Power Platform environment.

claims.claim: Only internal administrators can link the Business Central and Power Platform environments.
claims.quote: Link the Business Central environment to the Power Platform environment. Only internal admins can complete this task.

claims.claim: Without an enabled overage source, the environment is limited to allocated prepaid credits.
claims.quote: If no overage source is enabled, the environment can consume only its allocated prepaid credits.

claims.claim: Using the allocation API requires an app registration configured for Power Platform API.
claims.quote: An [app registration configured for Power Platform API](programmability-authentication-v2).

claims.claim: The API user needs Power Platform Administrator, Global Administrator or equivalent licensing and capacity permissions.
claims.quote: Sign in as a user with the **Power Platform Administrator** or **Global Administrator** role, or an equivalent role that can manage licensing and capacity.

claims.claim: The TenantPool enforcement rule maps to Draw from the available capacity in my tenant.
claims.quote: The **Draw from the available capacity in my tenant** option in the admin center maps to the `TenantPool` enforcement rule

claims.claim: Enabling TenantPool allows consumption of unallocated tenant capacity after the allocation is exhausted.
claims.quote: when it's enabled, the environment continues to draw from unallocated tenant capacity after its own allocation is exhausted

claims.claim: The allocation tutorial describes disabling TenantPool as capping the environment at its allocation.
claims.quote: when it's disabled, the environment is capped at its allocation.

claims.where: Governance controls; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Both Draw from the available capacity in my tenant and Bill to my pay-as-you-go billing plan must be cleared for an allocation-only cap.
claims.quote: Select **Bill to my pay-as-you-go billing plan** to let the environment continue usage through the selected billing plan.

claims.claim: A published environment group rule governing tenant-pool draw blocks individual overrides with TenantPoolLockedByPolicy.
claims.quote: Updates through the Power Platform admin center, Power Platform API, or administration SDKs are rejected with the `TenantPoolLockedByPolicy` error.

claims.claim: Capability changes may take effect immediately or require users to sign out and back in.
claims.quote: Some AI features take effect immediately, while others require users to sign out and sign in again.

claims.claim: Agent > Create opens the wizard, where Permissions > Manage permissions assigns permissions.
claims.quote: Under **Permissions**, use **Manage permissions** to add the permissions that the agent should have.

claims.claim: The Create agent wizard uses Profile (role) > Setup profile to assign a profile.
claims.quote: Under **Profile (role)**, use the **Setup profile** option to select the profile that determines what UI elements the agent can see and interact with.

claims.claim: Learn documents Agent.UpdateAccessControl for assigning agent permission sets.
claims.quote: Agent.UpdateAccessControl(AgentUserSecurityID, TempAccessControlBuffer);

claims.claim: Learn documents Agent.SetProfile for assigning an agent profile.
claims.quote: Agent.SetProfile(AgentUserSecurityID, 'ACCOUNTANT', SystemApplicationAppId);

claims.claim: AL agent configuration across application boundaries is restricted rather than an unrestricted administrator API.
claims.quote: Creating instances, tasks, messages and any configuration changes targeting an agent defined in a different application is blocked with an error.

claims.claim: The linked permission-assignment page explains how to assign a permission set to a user.
claims.quote:
You can assign permissions sets to users in two ways:

- From the **User Card** page, by selecting permission sets to assign to the user.
- From the **Permission Set by User** page, by selecting users that a permission set is assigned to.

claims.fix: Remove the checklist item beginning 'Grant agents only the permission sets'. The verified permissions discussion and wizard path can remain elsewhere.
